title: でも — “but / however” at the start of a sentence
summary: A conjunction placed at the start of a sentence to say something that goes against, or differs from, what came before. Very common in conversation.

patterns.gloss: Sentence. でも, sentence (高いです。でも、買います。)

body.p: Finish the first sentence, then start the next with でも. It works after both polite and plain sentences.
でも sounds natural in conversation. In essays and formal writing, しかし is the better choice.

body.h: Difference from が and けど
body.p: が and けど join two parts inside one sentence. でも starts a new sentence.

examples.ja: 高（たか）いです。でも、買（か）います。
examples.tr: It's expensive. But I'll buy it.

examples.ja: 疲（つか）れました。でも、まだ働（はたら）きます。
examples.tr: I'm tired. But I'll still work.

examples.ja: 雨（あめ）です。でも、出（で）かけます。
examples.tr: It's raining. But I'm going out.

pitfalls: Do not put it in the middle of a sentence. To link within one sentence, use けど or が.
In formal writing use しかし instead.
